scope: Primary curvature-aware 2.5D space-charge literature; no OPALX edits or new runs

papers.title: Two-and-a-half dimensional symplectic space-charge solver
papers.author: Ji Qiang
papers.version_note: The updated preprint explicitly describes minor improvements over the published paper. Published PDF has 25 pages; updated PDF has 26.
papers.author_claim_summary: Potential-derived kicks share one Hamiltonian. The zeroth-order solver neglects longitudinal potential curvature for smooth long bunches; iteration can restore it. Gaussian field comparisons vary gamma; the conclusion describes good agreement above beam-frame aspect ratio 1000. Curvature illustrations use 1 mm round Gaussian beams at h=1,0.1,0.01 per metre; the large-ring estimate is O(h sigma), about 1e-5 at R above 100 m.

published_locators.regularized_curvature_potential: Eq. 91; Appendix E, Eq. E11, p. 114602-24

updated_preprint_locators.free_space_reference_matching: Eqs. 48-54, pp. 8-9: r0 minimizes on-axis 2.5D/3D Gaussian longitudinal-field discrepancy; round long-bunch limit r0 approximately 1.1 gamma sigma_z

papers.version_specific_warning: The r0 matching/minimization section is present in the improved 2026 preprint and absent from the 2025 published PDF; do not assign its equation numbers or claim to the original version.
papers.not_demonstrated: No 1% finite hard-ended 143-degree uniform elliptical tube benchmark or full accelerator tracking validation appears in these illustrated field comparisons.

papers.title: Space charge modeling method in 2.5D for scaling fixed-field alternating-gradient accelerators
papers.read_scope: Primary accepted abstract only. No accessible manuscript or arXiv preprint located through the searched official links.
papers.author_claim_summary: PyFFA reconstructs a dynamic local slicing frame from an energy-dependent family of closed orbits, solves transverse Poisson equations there, and restores global cylindrical fields. The abstract reports analytical comparisons of fields, tune shifts, RMS envelopes and longitudinal phase space.
papers.limitations_of_available_evidence: The abstract does not provide radius, beta, source profile, error norm or a 1% bound. Those quantitative details cannot be inferred or substituted from the older proceedings.

papers.title: Modeling of long-bunch space charge in circular accelerators with unfixed closed orbit
papers.author_claim_summary: Static cylindrical slicing can misproject long arc bunches, causing artificial edge fields and emittance growth. PyFFAG maps particles and fields through an energy-dependent reference orbit. Its stated model uses transverse 2D Poisson and azimuthal 1D Poisson. Preliminary 1000-turn results vary bunch duration 80/120 ns and intensity 5e12/2e13 protons, reporting emittance and tune-shift trends.
papers.limitations: No finite-tube Coulomb end-field accuracy norm, matching R=2 m case or uniform 1% guarantee is provided. The manuscript labels development/validation preliminary.

our_case_independent_calculations.shape_note: Constant uniform line density has sigma_s=L/sqrt(12); uniform elliptical section has transverse RMS semiaxes/2. The physical Jacobian gives a tiny radial centroid correction, immaterial at displayed precision.

explicit_inferences_not_author_claims: Small h*x is a local transverse metric condition; a total bunch angle L/R of 2.5 radians does not itself violate h*x<<1. It does make a global Cartesian bunch interpretation inappropriate.
A sharp density step has arbitrarily short longitudinal scales. Therefore overall L/a=1000 does not establish the slow-variation assumption at its ends; our finite-end test probes that local failure.
Small potential or dominant-transverse-field corrections do not bound fractional error in the much smaller curvature-only on-axis radial field.

Qiang's displayed regularized Gaussian correction is proportional to x times an integral whose numerator vanishes quadratically at x=y=0. Its on-axis radial derivative therefore vanishes as written. It does not directly predict the sign or magnitude of our finite-tube on-axis hoop field; matching global geometry/boundaries would be necessary for that claim.
The geometry-remapping literature supports checking frame consistency separately from the physical end and curvature operator. Passing a mapping test does not establish finite-end Coulomb accuracy.
